$comment: Advisories the CI audit gate (scripts/audit-gate.mjs) tolerates. Each entry MUST carry a justification and a reviewBy date; the gate warns (does not fail) past reviewBy so releases can't be broken by a calendar, but the warning is the nudge to re-check upstream. Remove an entry the moment a fix ships.

allow.title: Immutable.js List 32-bit trie overflow DoS
allow.justification: immutable@3.8.3 is pinned by swagger-ui-react (latest 5.32.10 still requires ^3.x — no upstream fix exists, and overriding to immutable 4/5 breaks swagger-ui's redux-immutable internals). Exposure: immutable runs client-side in /api-docs rendering the app's OWN committed public/openapi.json — no attacker-controlled data reaches it, so the DoS vectors (huge Lists / crafted hash-collision keys) have no input path.

allow.title: Immutable.js Map/Set hash-collision algorithmic complexity DoS
allow.justification: Same pinned immutable@3.x via swagger-ui-react and same first-party-spec-only exposure as GHSA-v56q-mh7h-f735.

allow.title: brace-expansion DoS via unbounded expansion length (OOM crash)
allow.justification: NO PATCHED RELEASE EXISTS below 5.0.8: the advisory range is <=5.0.7, and 1.1.16 / 2.1.2 are the NEWEST releases in their lines (verified against the registry) — there is no 1.x/2.x/3.x/4.x backport. The remaining vulnerable copies are pinned transitively by minimatch@3.1.5 (^1.1.7) and minimatch@5.1.9 (^2.0.1), and cannot be overridden: brace-expansion 5.x moved its CJS export from a callable default to a named object ({EXPANSION_MAX, EXPANSION_MAX_LENGTH, expand}), so forcing 5.x into minimatch@3.1.5 (which does `var expand = require('brace-expansion')` then calls it) throws 'expand is not a function' — breaking lint AND electron-builder packaging. This is exactly why the overrides entry is scoped 'brace-expansion@>=3.0.0': it upgrades only consumers that already expect the named-export shape. Do not widen it. Exposure: NIL. Every glob pattern in the repo is first-party (eslint.config.mjs, electron-builder.yml) — no user input reaches a brace expansion. The only production chain is exceljs@4.4.0 -> archiver@5.3.2 -> {glob@7 -> minimatch@3.1.5, readdir-glob@1.1.3 -> minimatch@5.1.9}, and the vulnerable path requires archive.glob(), which exceljs never calls (verified: no '.glob(' anywhere in exceljs/lib) — the app uses only the jszip writer/reader (workbook.xlsx.writeBuffer / workbook.xlsx.load) in src/app/api/filaments/{export,import}-xlsx/route.ts. NOTE: npm reports fixAvailable eslint@10.8.0 for this advisory; that is WRONG — verified in a sandbox lockfile that the advisory PERSISTS after the eslint semver-major, so the upgrade is pure risk for zero benefit. Re-check when minimatch ships a release depending on brace-expansion >=5.0.8.
